page_title: Things to do in Patagonia: hiking, glaciers and wildlife
meta_description: What to do in Patagonia: hiking, glaciers, wildlife, boat trips, skiing and scenic drives. Where to do each activity and when.
hero_subtitle: Glaciers, mountains, lakes and wildlife: these are the experiences that define a trip to the far south.

categories.name: Hiking & trekking
categories.description: Patagonia has some of the world's most famous trails, with options for every level: from short walks to viewpoints to multi-day treks.
top_spots: Laguna de los Tres and Laguna Torre, El Chaltén

categories.name: Glaciers
categories.description: Seeing a glacier up close is one of the most powerful experiences of the trip: from walkways, on a boat in front of the ice walls or hiking on the glacier with guides.
categories.best_season: All year; more activities from October to April

categories.name: Wildlife
categories.description: Whales, penguins, sea lions, guanacos and condors. Patagonia is one of the best places in South America to see wildlife in the wild.
categories.best_season: Depends on the species: whales, roughly June to December

categories.name: Boat trips & kayaking
categories.description: Patagonia's lakes and channels can be explored by boat or kayak, surrounded by islands, forests and mountains.
top_spots: Victoria Island and Arrayanes Forest, Bariloche

categories.name: Skiing & snow
categories.description: In winter, Patagonia's ski resorts welcome skiers from around the world, with slopes overlooking lakes and forests.
top_spots: Cerro Chapelco, San Martín de los Andes
categories.best_season: June to September, depending on snow

categories.name: Scenic drives
categories.description: Some of the most beautiful scenery is enjoyed from the road, stopping at viewpoints, lakes and small towns.
top_spots: Route 40 between El Calafate and El Chaltén
categories.best_season: All year; take care with snow in winter

spring.name: Spring
spring.highlight: Whale season at Valdés Peninsula and the arrival of penguins on the coast.

summer.name: Summer
summer.highlight: Very long days and all trails and tours running. It's high season.

autumn.name: Autumn
autumn.highlight: Forests turn red and yellow and there are fewer visitors.

winter.name: Winter
winter.highlight: Snow in the Andes and ski season. Some trails and tours close.

practical_tips.title: Dress in layers
practical_tips.description: A single day can bring sun, wind, rain and cold. A good windbreaker is essential.

practical_tips.title: Book ahead
practical_tips.description: In high season, the most popular tours sell out weeks in advance.

practical_tips.title: Leave spare days
practical_tips.description: The weather is in charge. An extra day can save a hike or a boat trip.

practical_tips.title: Follow park rules
practical_tips.description: Stay on the trails, don't feed wildlife and pack out your waste.

closing: Patagonia is best enjoyed slowly. Choose a few bases, leave time for the weather and let it surprise you.
